text: {"frames":["\"Follow the blue light!\" calls Joop, as the lantern on the barge swings toward the canal under the Tower. The barge slides through the dark water past the mill, and a trail of small blue sparks marks the way on your plan. The route runs {a} cells along the quay, then {b} cells beside the locks, and {c|cell|cells|cells} more up to the gate that has been locked since yesterday. Every cell on the plan is {d} m on the ground, and the lantern will only go out once the gate knows how far it has come. How many metres long is the route?","The key rack in the market is empty except for one hook, and Femke wrings her apron in despair. Yesterday the keys hung there in a row, and this morning a tiny brass key lies on the herring barrel with no door to fit. The stallholder swears that the keys belong to doors that do not exist yet, and she points at the wall where a new door is starting to show. You turn the plan over and trace the passage that the keys must open. The passage runs {a} cells past the waffle stall, then {b} cells down the stairs, and {c|cell|cells|cells} cells more into the dark. Each cell is {d} m on the ground, so how many metres must you walk to reach the door?","Behind the cupboard in the hall, something scratches, so you pull the heavy wood aside. A door as tall as a cat stands in the wall, with a brass knob and a crack of warm light underneath. Bas says the door was not there yesterday, and that the mice have been keeping it open for a reason. You unroll the plan of the Tower and find a line that ends exactly at this door. The line runs {a} cells along the hall, {b} cells up the back stair, and {c|cell|cells|cells} cells across the attic. Every cell is {d} m on the ground, so how long is the way to the little door?","A faint tune drifts up through the floor boards, and the cheese smells sharper than usual. Anke says the music comes from the cheese cellar, where no one has been since the ice came. You take the lamp and follow the sound down the ladder, past the wheels of cheese stacked to the roof. The plan shows a passage that starts at the bottom step and runs away from the town. It goes {a} cells past the wheels, {b} cells under the canal, and {c|cell|cells|cells} cells more toward the music. Each cell on the plan is {d} m on the ground, so how far does the music lead you?","In the house with the hoist beam, every window glows yellow, yet the door is locked from inside and nobody answers. Lot presses her nose to the glass and sees a table laid for supper, with the chairs pulled out as if someone has just stood up. The light flickers, and a small bell rings on the sill. The plan of the Tower shows a route from the house to the mill, and the bell seems to be calling you along it. The route is {a} cells long on the quay, {b} cells over the bridge, and {c|cell|cells|cells} cells through the mill door. Every cell is {d} m on the ground, so how many metres does the bell want you to walk?"]}
